passages.title: The slow return of the night train
passages.text:
[A] For much of the twentieth century, travelling overnight by train was a normal way to cross a country or a continent. Passengers boarded in the evening, slept in narrow beds as the train moved through the dark, and woke up in another city in time for breakfast. In the early twenty-first century, however, many of these services were cut, and some railway companies predicted that the night train would soon belong only in history books. Today the picture is changing again, and new sleeper routes are being announced in several regions.

[B] The decline of the night train had several causes. Low-cost airlines made it possible to fly between major cities for less than the price of a sleeper ticket, and the journey took one hour instead of ten. At the same time, new high-speed railway lines allowed daytime trains to cover long distances quickly, so fewer travellers needed to spend a night on board. Sleeper carriages were also expensive to maintain, and because each passenger needs a bed rather than a seat, a night train carries far fewer people than a daytime service of the same length.

[C] What has brought the night train back is, above all, a change in how people think about travel. Surveys in several countries show that a growing number of travellers, particularly younger ones, are worried about the carbon emissions produced by flying. For a journey of around a thousand kilometres, a train produces only a small fraction of the emissions of a plane. Many travellers also point out that a night train saves the cost of a hotel and delivers them to the centre of a city, rather than to an airport far outside it.

[D] Expectations, however, have changed since the last generation of sleepers was built. Passengers who once accepted shared compartments with six narrow beds now want privacy, clean bathrooms and reliable wifi. Some new services offer small private cabins with a shower, while others have introduced capsule-style beds similar to those in budget hotels. Operators report that families and solo travellers are particularly interested in cabins that can be locked from the inside.

[E] Meeting these expectations is not easy, because many operators are still using carriages that are thirty or forty years old. Old heating systems break down in winter, and spare parts for some models are no longer manufactured. One operator was forced to cancel a popular route for an entire season when three of its carriages failed safety inspections. New carriages are being built, but each one takes years to design and approve, and they cost several million euros.

[F] International routes face additional difficulties. Each country has its own railway rules, electricity systems and safety standards, so a train that crosses several borders may need to change locomotives and drivers along the way. Timetables must also be agreed between national companies with different priorities. A delay in one country can cause a train to miss its time slot in the next, leaving passengers to arrive hours late.

[G] For the companies that run them, night trains are a difficult business. Because each carriage holds relatively few people, a train needs to be almost completely full every night to cover its costs. Operators have tried to increase income by selling food and drinks on board and by offering cheaper seats in carriages without beds. Even so, few routes make a profit, and most rely on some form of public money.

[H] Whether the revival continues will therefore depend largely on governments. Supporters argue that public funding is justified because night trains reduce emissions and connect smaller cities that airlines ignore. Critics reply that the money would achieve more if it were spent on improving daytime services used by far larger numbers of people. For now, demand is strong, and many new routes are fully booked months in advance – but the night train’s long-term future is far from guaranteed.

coach.message: Bài “Matching headings — night train revival”: Tìm ý chính duy nhất của mỗi đoạn và loại heading trùng ý. Trước khi thử, hãy nói một việc bạn sẽ kiểm tra ở bài này.

Bạn đang xem “high-speed rail” (noun phrase), nghĩa là “đường sắt cao tốc”. Ví dụ: “High-speed rail reduced travel times.”. Hãy tạo một câu mới liên quan đến matching headings — night train revival thay vì chép lại.

Ở ví dụ có hướng dẫn “Choose the best heading: A Luxury sleeping arrangements / B Restored links between smaller towns / C Tourist…”, hãy làm bước này trước: Dự đoán ý chính trước khi dò lựa chọn, nhưng không đoán đáp án khi chưa có bằng chứng. Chỉ mở mẫu sau khi tự thử.

Lỗi dễ gặp ở bài “Matching headings — night train revival”: Không xem chi tiết dễ hình dung (comfortable cabins) là ý chính. “But its most important achievement” báo hiệu trọng tâm của đoạn. Cabin và tour operators chỉ bổ sung; B tóm…

Bạn đã hoàn thành bài “Matching headings — night train revival”. Hãy đánh dấu bằng chứng trong văn bản; lưu cụm “high-speed rail” nếu thực sự muốn dùng lại, rồi sửa một chỗ chưa chắc chắn trước khi làm bài mới.
Bài này mình luyện Matching Headings – Night trains. Hãy đọc đoạn rồi tìm phần nào trả lời đúng câu hỏi; chưa cần đoán ngay.
Bạn đang bị bẫy: Environmental benefits: thuộc C, không phải B. Hãy đọc bằng chứng “Budget flights made overnight services less competitive” rồi thử lại.
Hãy phân biệt: Old carriage problems: là nội dung đoạn B. Bằng chứng cần đối chiếu là “reduce travel emissions”.
Bạn đã tìm đúng cả hai bằng chứng. Hãy vào phần luyện độc lập; Coach sẽ không tự chen vào.

Ở bài Matching Headings: main idea vs example, trước tiên thử trả lời: Choose the best heading: A Luxury sleeping arrangements / B Restored links between smaller towns / C Tourist advertising. Đừng đoán vội; mình sẽ chỉ cách tìm dấu hiệu.
Hãy thử dùng “high-speed rail” trong một câu. Cụm này là noun phrase, nghĩa là đường sắt cao tốc.
Gợi ý ngay trong ví dụ: Vượt giới hạn từ bị chấm sai dù ý đúng. Hãy tìm điểm đó trong câu trước khi mở đáp án.
Lỗi thường gặp ở bài này: Không xem chi tiết dễ hình dung (comfortable cabins) là ý chính. Hãy sửa theo nguyên tắc: Yet signals the contrast: operations are costly but passenger demand rises.
Giờ kiểm lại cách làm Matching Headings: main idea vs example: đối chiếu câu hỏi, lý do và nguồn. Thử câu mới: Underline the contrast marker, then write a heading in your own words.
